$comment: Single source for UI coverage of the API. docs/ui-spec.md explains the areas and the reasoning; tools/prove-ui-covers-the-api.php checks this file against openapi.json in both directions, and tools/prove-screens-call-their-operations.php checks it against the frontend — that every area's routes exist and that every operation an area claims is actually called through the generated client.

authorities.$comment: Which authority a screen answers to, not which shell it lives in — there has been one shell since ADR-046. The same three words the navigation uses, so the file and the code describe the boundary in one vocabulary instead of two.
authorities.tenant: Answers to a tenant's membership. One product, scoped by X-Product and by what the caller's membership grants (`GET /me/permissions`).
authorities.platform: Answers to a platform role. Never derived from a membership and never granting one (non-negotiable #22); a separate catalogue, a separate identity (`GET /staff/me`), and every read that crosses into tenant data is traced.
authorities.public: Answers to no authority. The shop window and signing up: the person reading has no session, no product and no permissions, so nothing here may depend on any.

account.profile.$comment: Since 2026-09-23 it also offers a new password, by asking for the same emailed link the sign-in screen offers somebody locked out. `forgotPassword` stays claimed by `identity.sign_in` and is listed there once: it is one operation with one meaning, and there is deliberately no second mechanism for a person who is already signed in — the link proves the address, and following it revokes every session (ADR-038).

commerce.catalogue.$comment: What a product sells, and the one acquisition that happens here rather than through the checkout: startFreemium (spec §6). A free period raises no order, no invoice and no payment — nothing is outstanding, so nothing is raised — and the button for it is on the card that advertises it, beside Souscrire. Everything with a price goes to commerce.checkout. Since étape 7 (spec §7) the rows also *change* what is already held — previewOfferChange, changeOffer, scheduleOfferChange, cancelScheduledChange, showSchedule and cancelSubscription — and those stay claimed by tenant.subscription, which is where they are the subject rather than an offer's consequence: an operation has one home in this map, and gate:screens checks that the frontend calls it, not from which screen.

console.admin.catalogue.$comment: The platform pricing its own product. ADR-040 made catalog.manage a delegation to a tenant, which left the platform able to price its own catalogue only by lending it away and acting as the borrower; and plans could not be created at all, so a fresh installation had a product it could not price. Plans, offers and versions, with the product taken from the switcher because the console has no ambient product. Features are no longer here: they are the platform's one list, under console.admin.features.

console.admin.showcase.$comment: The story a product tells on its own page (2026-09-24, docs/home-showcase-spec.md). Written by the platform's own staff under staff.products.manage and never by a tenant: a page written by one customer would be read by every other customer of the same product (§11.1). Writing and publishing are separate acts, so four bands can be written over an afternoon without a stranger reading the half-finished ones. The editor is driven by the same block registry the page renders from, so a band added tomorrow gets its form by existing. Since 2026-09-26 this area is not the only caller of showProductStory and writeProductStory: console.admin.translations lists every sentence of every story and saves one through this pair, re-reading the story and sending all of it back, because there is no route that writes one band. It stays claimed here, which is where the permission and the trail are.

console.admin.features.$comment: The platform's one list of features (2026-09-24, docs/translatable-fields-spec.md §4). A feature is not a thing a product owns; it is a word the platform and a product's code have agreed on, and max_projects existed once per product until this screen. No product is named here, which is the whole point: a product's catalogue picks a code from this list. Retiring replaces deleting, because a feature some offer version grants can never be removed.

console.admin.translations.$comment: Everything the operator wrote, in every language it has (2026-09-26). The console could already translate these one at a time — a feature on the Features screen, an offer on the Catalogue, a band on the product's Story screen — each behind the form that owns its row. What no screen could answer is the question somebody asks when a language is half finished: what is missing in Italian? That answer spans tables with nothing else in common, so it needs a read that does too. This is the *operator's* words and not the application's: labels, buttons and error wording live in the bundle's JSON catalogues, keyed by the English and proved complete by gate:i18n (ADR-050, docs/translatable-fields-spec.md §1.5), and this screen is not a reason to move them. It reads listTranslations and writes through renameFeature, renameStaffOffer and writeProductStory, which are claimed by the screens that own those rows: one operation, one owner, and no second way to write the same table. The product showcase joined the desk on 2026-09-26 (translatable-fields-spec §5.1) and is the reason writeProductStory is in that list: it replaces a product's whole story, so this screen re-reads the story from showProductStory at the moment it saves and sends all of it back. Both of those operations stay claimed by console.admin.showcase, which owns them.

console.admin.directory.$comment: The cross-tenant view, and since 2026-09-26 it finally answers the other half of a bill. listAdminInvoices says what was owed; listAdminPayments says whether it arrived — the operator could read every document ever raised and not one payment against one of them, so "did this customer actually pay?" had no screen. The payments rows name the customer out of the invoice's own snapshot (§25) and leave the number null while that invoice is a draft, for the reason a gapless sequence exists.

console.admin.invoicing.$comment: A product's configuration desk. ADR-042 gave the console a way to create a product and ADR-043 a way to price it, and a checkout against one created that way still refused with BILLING_NOT_CONFIGURED: an invoice must name its issuer, and the issuer lives in product_configuration, which only the demo seeder ever wrote. Three named keys rather than a JSONB editor, because every key in that table is read by code that names it and a typo would store configuration nothing reads. The third, project_schema_versions, closed the same hole one layer down (2026-09-29): creating a product wrote no configuration at all, and a product that has declared no versions accepts no project of any version. It sits here and not on the Products screen because showStaffConfiguration is the read that carries it, and two screens fetching one desk is how two answers to one question start. showProductManifest joined it on 2026-10-01 and is a fourth kind of thing: the only staff read that leaves this host. The product serves what it accepts at its own /.well-known/product.json, the screen shows that beside what the database holds, and applying stays the deliberate PUT — a fetch that wrote would let a product's host re-open a version the platform had retired. It is fetched on its own and never with the configuration beside it, so a product whose server is down does not make the billing settings unopenable.

console.self.$comment: A platform staff member's own profile (2026-09-22): name, language, and since 2026-09-23 a new password by the same emailed link as everybody else — staff sign in with an address and a password, so the link belongs to the account rather than to the authority (see `account.profile`). `account.profile` is a tenant screen and staff with no membership were refused it, which left the platform administrator with no way to their own name or language. The identity itself is bootstrap (showStaffIdentity).

console.admin.demo.$comment: The demonstration, on a screen of its own (2026-09-18): the public /demo page's switch (staff.demo.publish) and the reset of the demonstration world (staff.demo.reset, refused while a product that is not the demo's exists). Neither is administering products, where both used to sit.

console.admin.products.$comment: The top of the model. A product is what tenants belong to and what offers are priced for, and until this screen existed only the installer could create one and nothing at all could list them — listProducts resolves through membership, which a platform role never grants. There is no delete: a product carries invoices, and an invoice is a legal document. The demonstration world is reset from here too, behind staff.demo.reset: the products are what it is made of, and it is refused while one that is not the demo's exists.

console.admin.menus.$comment: What the shell shows each kind of person — platform administrator, tenant administrator, user — chosen by the platform administrator on 2026-09-17, platform-wide. Three checklists of the shell's own entries and, per audience, whether an entry with nothing behind it is shown at all. Hiding is courtesy, as it is for permissions; a section with no remaining entries disappears.

console.admin.readiness.$comment: The console's landing and the map of a maze. A fresh installation was navigable only by walking into its refusals — no plan so no offer, published but not advertised so an empty shop window, a checkout refusing with BILLING_NOT_CONFIGURED at the very end. Every refusal correct, together a maze. The chain is returned in dependency order so working down it never meets one, and the facts are read through the same ports the enforcing code reads.

console.admin.staff.$comment: Who holds platform authority. The screen that stops a fresh installation being a dead end: before it, appointing anybody meant an INSERT against production, which is exactly what an installer must never require.

console.admin.mail.$comment: The words the platform's mails say, and a test of the mail host (2026-09-19). Behind staff.mail.manage. The four mails a person acts on from an inbox are editable, with placeholders; everything else keeps a generic rendering. The test is sent inside the request, to the caller's own address, so the mail host's answer is seen now.

console.admin.palette.$comment: The design system and its palettes (2026-10-04), behind staff.design.manage, which PLATFORM_ADMIN alone holds. /console/palette is index.css read at build time — mood board in both themes, colour groups, fonts, type scale, contrast — and can save what it read as a palette. /console/palettes edits the palettes, and holds the matrix: organisations by product, each cell the palette worn where the organisation holds the product. Only the platform administrator changes a palette; the assignment is one row, also written by the organisation's own screen (tenant.palette).

console.admin.storefront.$comment: What the public page advertises, and what a stranger has to do to get past it. Behind staff.catalog.manage rather than catalog.manage: ADR-040 lets the platform lend the latter to a tenant, and a tenant authoring its own offers must not decide what a stranger is shown. The product it administers is the one chosen in the context bar's switcher, which on the console lists every product the platform hosts (ADR-047): a platform role grants no membership, so the choice is made from the platform's own list rather than from what somebody belongs to. The sign-up settings (ADR-063) are on this screen because the front door is what it describes, and behind staff.sign_up.manage rather than the screen's own permission: being shown an offer and having to prove an address are two trusts, and the panel is absent for somebody holding only the other one.

console.support.tenants.$comment: A tenant as support sees it, and the two things the platform may change about them: which products they hold (ADR-047), and whether the catalogue is lent to them. Both sit here rather than on a screen of their own because the decision is made while looking at the customer it concerns.

console.support.tenant.$comment: One customer, read from the console with the tenant and product pickers in the bar: who belongs to it (members), what it subscribed to and what it was invoiced, per product. Read-only by construction — a platform role never edits a membership (#22) — and every read carries the motive R14 asks for and lands in the access log. Payments, orders, quotes, projects, jobs and the fiscal identity read the same way; support threads through listSupportConversations with its tenant filter.

identity.sign_in.$comment: The screen U11 found missing and U12 made this platform's own. It has a route so it is addressable and so this area can declare one, but nothing links to it: SignInGate renders it *instead of* the shell for whatever URL was asked for, which is how a deep link survives signing in. It also answers the confirmation link: verifying an address is something somebody does from a device that has never signed in, so it belongs on the one screen that works without a session.

public.demo.$comment: The demonstration page (2026-09-18): what the platform hosts, who is in it and as what, to anybody — off until a platform administrator switches it on from the Demonstration screen (setDemoPage), and a 404 while it is off. Outside both shells and the sign-in gate, like the storefront; a link to each organisation's root is what it offers next.

public.storefront.$comment: The landing page and the account it creates. The product is chosen from listPublicProducts — only products with something advertised, so the list says nothing the windows do not (ADR-047) — or named by ?product=, never taken from a membership; and only offers marked publicly_listed appear — being on sale and being advertised are two different decisions. Choosing an offer opens the sign-up form; the checkout that follows runs on the session that creates and is therefore commerce.checkout's openCheckoutSession, not a second anonymous purchase flow with rules of its own. Since 2026-10-04 the page wears the palette the organisation chose for the product (getPublicPalette) — the same one its members see.

tenant.palette.$comment: Which palette the organisation's screens wear in this product (2026-10-04). It chooses among the platform's palettes and never edits one — palettes are the platform administrator's. The same row the console's matrix writes, so each side sees what the other chose. Behind skin.manage alone, tied to no offer. Reading what the screens wear is bootstrap, because every member's shell reads it to paint itself.

organisation.subscriptions.$comment: Who in the organisation holds what, with the places taken (2026-09-25). Its own area rather than a corner of tenant.subscription: a different permission (tenant.manage) and a different question — that one answers for whoever is asking, this one for everybody. Read-only until 2026-09-30, when it gained the one thing an administrator may change about somebody else's subscription: whether they are on it themselves. Not who else is on it — that stays the owner's decision — and it spends no place, because an administrator takes none.

bootstrap.$comment: Read by the shell to decide what exists for this person: which navigation entries appear, which actions are enabled, which empty state is honest. Not screens.

not_in_ui.getPublicShowcaseAsset: The bytes of a picture on a published product page (2026-09-24). Reached by the browser as an whose address the *server* composed — both showProductStory and getPublicShowcase answer it as a field — so the generated client never fetches these bytes itself and no screen spells the route. The same story as downloadAsset, minus the signature: the reader has no session to mint one with, and the page is public by the operator's own act.
not_in_ui.downloadAsset: Reached by browser navigation on a signed link that createAssetLink produced; the generated client never fetches these bytes itself.
not_in_ui.einvoiceWebhook: Server-to-server callback from the e-invoicing platform. No human origin, so no screen.
not_in_ui.health: Monitoring probe consumed by infrastructure, not by a person.
not_in_ui.paymentWebhook: Server-to-server callback from the payment provider. No human origin, so no screen.
not_in_ui.listProductTenantMembers: Called by a product’s server with its key and no person present (ADR-051 §4); the console issues the key, the product access log records the read. No human origin, so no screen.
not_in_ui.reportProductUsage: Called by a product’s server with its key, before it does the metered work (ADR-051 §4). No human origin, so no screen.
not_in_ui.declareProductCapabilities: Called by a product’s server with its key, on deployment, to say what it gates on (2026-09-24, ADR-052). No human origin, so no screen — and deliberately none: a console form here would be a second place the same list is written, and the point of the route is that the program declaring it is the authority on what it built. Every code is checked against the platform’s list, which a person does keep on a screen — console.admin.features.
not_in_ui.showProductTenantEntitlements: Called by a product’s server with its key and no person present (ADR-051 §4). No human origin, so no screen.
not_in_ui.getJwks: The public keys sessions are signed with (ADR-051 milestone E), read by a product’s server that verifies bearers locally. The shell never verifies a token — it presents one — so there is no screen.
not_in_ui.showMyContext: Read by a product deployed beside the platform (ADR-051 §3) — its server asks who is asking and what they hold, in one call, instead of verifying the token itself. The shell reads the same facts through showMe, showMyPermissions and showMyEntitlements and needs no fourth screen for them.
